content:
We need to produce a resume for Matthias Algiers. Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but ensure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times. So we can have up to 9 uppercase words. We must wrap the entire response with double quotation marks. So output must be a single string enclosed in double quotes, containing the resume text. Inside that, we can have uppercase words for highlighting key abilities, but must ensure total count of uppercase words (i.e., words that are all capital letters) is less than 10. We can include maybe 5 uppercase words.

We must not add commentary about constraints. Just output the resume wrapped in double quotes.

We need to ensure that the uppercase words are actual words, like "LEADERSHIP", "PROJECT MANAGEMENT"? But that is two words; each word must be all caps. We can have uppercase words like "EXPERTISE", "STRATEGIC", "INNOVATIVE", "ANALYTICAL", "COMMUNICATION". That's 5. Ensure they appear less than 10 times. Also we must be careful not to accidentally have other words all caps like "AND" or "THE". So we should avoid using all caps for common words. So we must write the resume in normal sentence case, except we insert some uppercase words for highlighting.

We must wrap entire response with double quotation marks. So output starts with a double quote, ends with a double quote, and inside is the resume.

We need to ensure that the double quotes are only at the start and end, not inside. If we need to include internal quotes, we might break the rule. Safer to avoid internal double quotes. Use single quotes if needed, but better avoid quotes inside.

Thus produce something like:

"Matthias Algiers
[Contact info]
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY: ... 
KEY SKILLS: EXPERTISE in ... STRATEGIC planning, INNOVATIVE problem solving, ANALYTICAL thinking, COMMUNICATION abilities.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE: ...
..."

We need to count uppercase words: EXPERTISE, STRATEGIC, INNOVATIVE, ANALYTICAL, COMMUNICATION = 5. Ensure no other uppercase words appear inadvertently. We must avoid using all caps for things like "PDF", "USA", "CEO", etc. So avoid those. Also avoid acronyms like "HR", "IT". Use lowercase.

Make sure not to accidentally have words like "AND" in caps; we will keep them lowercase.

We need to ensure that the uppercase words appear as separate tokens, not attached to punctuation that might make them not considered a word? Probably they count as words if they are all caps letters. So we should avoid punctuation attached directly without space? Eg "EXPERTISE," with a comma after might still be considered a word? Safer to put them without trailing punctuation, or ensure punctuation separated by space. We'll put them followed by a space then comma.

E.g., "EXPERTISE ," but that looks odd. Better: "EXPERTISE," maybe still considered a word with punctuation attached; but the instruction likely counts the word token ignoring punctuation. Safer to put them without punctuation attached: "EXPERTISE" then a space then continue.

We can do: "KEY SKILLS: EXPERTISE in STRATEGIC planning, INNOVATIVE problem solving, ANALYTICAL thinking, COMMUNICATION abilities." Here we have uppercase words: EXPERTISE, STRATEGIC, INNOVATIVE, ANALYTICAL, COMMUNICATION. That's 5. Ensure no other uppercase.

Now check for any accidental uppercase: "Matthias Algiers" - both capitalized first letters but not all caps. "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY:" - "PROFESSIONAL" is all caps! That's an uppercase word we didn't intend to count. That would add to count. We must avoid any all caps words besides the selected ones. So we need to avoid using all caps for section headings. Use normal case for headings: "Professional Summary:", "Key Skills:", "Professional Experience:", "Education:", etc. Ensure they are not all caps.

Thus we need to rewrite resume with normal case headings.

We also must avoid words like "USA", "PDF". Use lowercase.

Now produce resume.

Let's craft:

"Matthias Algiers
Email: matthias.algiers@example.com | Phone: (555) 123-4567 | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/matthiasalgiers

Professional Summary
Results-driven professional with over 8 years of experience in project management and strategic planning. Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams, deliver complex projects on time and within budget, and drive continuous improvement through innovative solutions.

Key Skills
EXPERTISE in STRATEGIC planning, INNOVATIVE problem solving, ANALYTICAL thinking, COMMUNICATION abilities
Project lifecycle management
Stakeholder engagement
Risk assessment and mitigation
Data-driven decision making
Agile and Waterfall methodologies

Professional Experience
Senior Project Manager, TechNova Solutions, Austin, TX — March 2020 – Present
- Directed portfolios of up to 15 simultaneous projects, achieving a 95% on-time delivery rate.
- Championed the adoption of Agile frameworks, reducing cycle time by 20%.
- Facilitated workshops that enhanced team collaboration and increased stakeholder satisfaction scores by 30%.
- Managed budgets exceeding $2M, optimizing resource allocation and cutting costs by 12%.

Project Manager, Global Dynamics Corp, Dallas, TX — June 2015 – February 2020
- Led end-to-end execution of infrastructure upgrades, improving system reliability by 25%.
- Coordinated with vendors and internal teams to ensure compliance with industry standards.
- Produced detailed performance reports that informed executive strategy adjustments.
- Mentored junior staff, fostering a culture of continuous learning and professional growth.

Education
Master of Business Administration, University of Texas at Austin — Graduated 2015
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Texas A&M University — Graduated 2012

Certifications
Project Management Professional (PMP) – PMI
Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) – Scrum Alliance"

Now check for any all caps words besides the five we intended.

We have "EXPERTISE", "STRATEGIC", "INNOVATIVE", "ANALYTICAL", "COMMUNICATION". That's 5.

Check other lines: "Results-driven" not all caps. "Professional Summary" - "Professional" not all caps (first letter capital, rest lowercase). "Summary" same. "Key Skills" - "Key" not all caps, "Skills" not all caps. "Senior Project Manager" - each word capitalized but not all caps. "TechNova Solutions" - contains mixed case but not all caps. "Austin, TX" - "TX" is all caps! That's a problem. "TX" is an abbreviation for Texas, all caps, counts as an uppercase word. We must avoid any all caps words besides the five we intend. So we need to avoid "TX". Use lowercase "tx"? But that's not standard. Could write "Texas" instead of "TX". So replace "TX" with "Texas". Similarly "TX" appears elsewhere.

Also "PMP" is all caps, "CSM" all caps. Those are acronyms we need to avoid. We can write them lowercase or avoid them. Maybe we can write "Project Management Professional (PMP)" but that includes "PMP" all caps. We could write "Project Management Professional certification" without the acronym. Or we could write "pmp" lowercase but that looks odd. Better to avoid the acronym entirely. So we can list certifications without the acronym: "Project Management Professional certification" and "Certified ScrumMaster certification". Ensure not to have all caps.

Also "Bachelor of Science" - "B.S." would be all caps if we used abbreviation; we wrote out full.

Now check for any other all caps like "USA", "IT", "HR". Not present.

Now check "March 2020 – Present": "Present" capitalized first letter only, not all caps.

Check "June 2015 – February 2020": fine.

Check "Master of Business Administration": fine.

Check "University of Texas at Austin": "University" capitalized, "Texas" capitalized, "Austin" capitalized but not all caps.

Check "Texas A&M University": "Texas" capitalized, "A&M" includes uppercase letters and ampersand, but "A&M" is not all caps because includes ampersand; but the letters A and M are uppercase, but there is an ampersand; still it's not all letters? It has uppercase letters and a symbol. Probably not considered a word with all capital letters because of the ampersand. Safer to avoid "A&M". Could write "Texas A and M University" but that's weird. Maybe we can keep it; it's not all caps because includes &. The instruction: "words with all capital letters" likely means consisting only of uppercase letters A-Z. So "A&M" includes a non-letter, so not counted. So okay.

Now check for "PMP" and "CSM": we need to remove or lowercase. Let's rewrite Certifications section:

"Certifications
Project Management Professional certification
